title: Utilization Management Policy — Long-Distance and Out-of-State RideLink Trips
content:
This policy governs Non-Emergency Medical Transportation trips beyond a RideLink level's standard one-way distance, and trips to providers out of state. The distances and lead times named are the level's own long-distance terms.

## In force

A trip whose one-way miles exceed the level's standard one-way limit is long distance and is booked only when requested at least the level's long-distance lead time in business days before the appointment and the treating provider confirms that no qualified provider is nearer; an out-of-state trip also needs plan approval where the level requires it.

| Condition for a long-distance trip | Required |
|---|---|
| Requested at least the lead time in business days before the appointment | Yes |
| Treating provider confirms no qualified provider is nearer | Yes |
| Plan approval, when the provider is out of state and the level requires it | Yes |

All the conditions that apply to the trip must hold together for it to be booked.

*Hypothetical, a level with a 50-mile standard limit:* a 50-mile one-way trip is not long distance; a 51-mile one-way trip is.

## No longer in force

The clause under which, for an approved long-distance trip of at least the level's lodging threshold one way, lodging up to the level's nightly lodging allowance per night and meals up to the level's daily meals allowance per travel day were reimbursed as a lodging and meals reimbursement (the amount being the lodging nights times the nightly allowance plus the meal days times the daily allowance) is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis for lodging and meals on a long-distance stay.

superseded_clauses: For an approved long-distance trip of at least lodging_threshold_miles one way, lodging up to lodging_per_night_usd per night and meals up to meals_per_day_usd per travel day are reimbursed as a lodging_meals reimbursement.
